content_units: Dinner Shortlist for 4 Under $35
A practical mix of fast, budget-friendly vegetarian dinners that also work for   1 gluten-free eater   with simple ingredient swaps or naturally gluten-free bases.
Best 5 Dinner Options
Option 1:   Black Bean Taco Bowls     Fast rice bowls with beans, corn, salsa, avocado, and toppings     Est. cost: $14–$18
-   Protein source:   Black beans, cheese or Greek yogurt if desired
-   Prep time:   25–30 min
-   Why it works:   Naturally easy to keep gluten-free by serving over rice instead of tortillas; vegetarian by default; everyone can customize toppings.
Build this meal
Option 2:   Red Lentil Coconut Curry with Rice     One-pot lentil curry with spinach or peas over rice     Est. cost: $12–$16
-   Protein source:   Red lentils
-   Prep time:   30–35 min
-   Why it works:   Naturally vegetarian and gluten-free if using certified GF spices/broth; no mushrooms needed; very filling at low cost.
View curry idea
Option 3:   Chickpea Pasta Primavera     Chickpea pasta with zucchini, tomatoes, spinach, garlic, and parmesan     Est. cost: $16–$22
-   Protein source:   Chickpea pasta, parmesan
-   Prep time:   25–35 min
-   Why it works:   Chickpea pasta gives a gluten-free option for everyone without making two meals; vegetarian, quick, and easy to scale.
Pasta base
Option 4:   Tofu Veggie Fried Rice     Rice, tofu, carrots, peas, eggs optional, and tamari     Est. cost: $13–$19
-   Protein source:   Tofu, eggs optional
-   Prep time:   30–40 min
-   Why it works:   Vegetarian and gluten-free if you use tamari instead of soy sauce; no mushrooms required; great for using affordable frozen vegetables.
Fried rice guide
Option 5:   Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Chili Beans     Baked or microwaved sweet potatoes topped with seasoned beans, salsa, and cheese     Est. cost: $12–$17
-   Protein source:   Pinto or black beans, cheese or yogurt
-   Prep time:   35–45 min
-   Why it works:   Naturally gluten-free, vegetarian, inexpensive, and easy to adjust toppings for different preferences.
Meal inspiration
Cost and Fit Comparison
Option   Estimated Cost   Protein Source   Prep Time   Why it fits mixed dietary needs
Black Bean Taco Bowls   $14–$18   Black beans, cheese   25–30 min   Rice base keeps it GF; customizable toppings suit everyone
Red Lentil Coconut Curry   $12–$16   Red lentils   30–35 min   Naturally vegetarian and GF-friendly with simple label checks
Chickpea Pasta Primavera   $16–$22   Chickpea pasta, parmesan   25–35 min   One pasta works for both vegetarian and GF needs
Tofu Veggie Fried Rice   $13–$19   Tofu, optional eggs   30–40 min   Use tamari for GF; easy mushroom-free vegetable mix
Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Chili Beans   $12–$17   Beans, cheese   35–45 min   Naturally GF, filling, and easy to customize
Smartest Picks for Your Constraints
-   Best overall:     Black Bean Taco Bowls
Cheapest flexible option, very quick, and easiest for mixed preferences.
-   Best high-protein budget pick:     Red Lentil Coconut Curry
Excellent cost-to-protein ratio and uses inexpensive pantry ingredients.
-   Best if you want one unified GF meal:     Chickpea Pasta Primavera
No separate gluten-free portion needed.
Planning Notes for Your Grocery Run

Using U.S. budget-store pricing, these estimates assume basics like oil, salt, and common spices are already on hand. For gluten-free safety, check packaged items such as   tamari, broth, spice blends, salsa, and pasta   for GF labeling if needed.
